title: A club built on good company.
lead: Since 1960, a shared love of the Corvette has brought people together across the Quad Cities and beyond.

sections.title: Corvettes, friends, community.
paragraphs: Mid-West Corvettes, Inc. is an Illinois not-for-profit club organized around the enjoyment of the Chevrolet Corvette. Our members make room for everything from a scenic drive and a relaxed lunch to rallies, car shows, and helping our neighbors.
We are a charter member of the National Council of Corvette Clubs. Our home is the Quad Cities, with members and activities on both sides of the Mississippi.

sections.title: A place to start
paragraphs: Come to a monthly meeting as our guest. You can meet the members, learn about upcoming activities, and decide whether the club is right for you.

title: Your next chapter starts here.
lead: Bring your Corvette enthusiasm. We’ll help you find the people, outings, and friendships that make MWC your own.

sections.title: Visit a meeting
paragraphs: Prospective members are welcome on the first Tuesday of the month at 6:30 pm at Eriksen Chevrolet, 325 1st Ave E, Milan, Illinois. Join us as a guest, ask questions, and get to know the club. Many members gather for dinner afterward.

sections.title: Make it official
paragraphs: When you’re ready, complete both the MWC and NCCC applications. Bring them to a meeting; board members can also provide forms and help you through the process. Contact our membership director for current dues and application questions.

title: The miles behind us.
lead: One idea, a handful of Corvette owners, and a friendship that has carried through generations.

sections.title: It started with Paul Castle
paragraphs: In 1960, 22-year-old Paul Castle set out to organize a club for Corvette owners. The first organizational meeting was held on May 15, 1960. His announcement described a club devoted to safe sporting and social activities centered on the Corvette.

title: Take the long way together.
lead: A favorite road is even better with a few Corvettes in the mirrors.

sections.title: An outing for your schedule
paragraphs: Club drive-outs range from a few hours to several days. Same-day trips often combine scenic roads, a stop to stretch, and a meal together. Longer adventures leave time to explore a region and enjoy an evening with the group.

sections.title: Spring, summer, and fall
paragraphs: Past trips have included Wisconsin and Minnesota in spring, Clear Lake in summer, and fall drives toward Winona or the Lake of the Ozarks. These are examples from the club’s travel history; this year’s plans and reservations are in the calendar.

sections.title: Before you leave
paragraphs: Check the event listing for the meeting point and drivers’ briefing. Bring a charged handheld two-way radio so the group can share road information. Ask the organizer about radio settings and the current drive-out procedures.

sections.title: Have a route in mind?
paragraphs: Members help shape the outings. If you have a favorite road, restaurant, or destination, bring the idea to the club.

title: Two seats. One shared challenge.
lead: Follow the clues, work with your navigator, and enjoy the road along the way.

sections.title: What is a road rally?
paragraphs: A road rally follows instructions over public roads at legal speeds. It is a navigation and observation challenge, not a race. Some formats also ask teams to follow a timetable or match a measured distance.

sections.title: The spring tradition
paragraphs: The Alan Fiscus Memorial Spring Rally helps open the club’s driving season. The club’s description includes route-and-observation challenges, poker stops, and a mileage challenge, with proceeds supporting club charity. Check the current event listing for the format, entry details, and date.

sections.title: Bring your navigator
paragraphs: Read the instructions together and bring something to write with. For timed formats, bring a watch that can be synchronized to the event time. The organizer’s briefing explains the route and scoring.

image.alt: The first Mid-West Corvettes fall rally in 1960
image.caption: The rally tradition reaches back to the club’s first year, 1960.

title: A little friendly competition.
lead: Explore your Corvette’s handling on a course built for the occasion.

sections.title: Low-speed, also called autocross
paragraphs: Drivers follow a course of cones across a paved lot, navigating turns and slaloms against the clock. Runs are electronically timed. MWC’s annual event has traditionally taken place during the summer.

sections.title: A day at the course
paragraphs: The club describes its autocross as an NCCC-sanctioned event, with points and trophies. The current event instructions determine participation requirements, registration, and the day’s schedule.

sections.title: Interested in taking part?
paragraphs: Check the calendar and contact the club’s speed director with questions before attending.

title: A Corvette-sized welcome.
lead: For the people along the route and the members behind the wheel, this is a day to enjoy together.

sections.title: Part of the celebration
paragraphs: MWC has participated in Memorial Day and Fourth of July parades on both sides of the Mississippi, along with the Tug Fest parade in Le Claire. A line of Corvettes makes a memorable addition to a hometown celebration.

sections.title: The fun carries on
paragraphs: Members often get together for a meal after the parade. Check the calendar for this year’s participation, staging location, arrival time, and organizer’s instructions.

image.alt: Mid-West Corvettes participating in a Fourth of July parade

title: Pull up a chair.
lead: The friendships keep going long after the cars are parked.

sections.title: Good company, all year
paragraphs: The club gets together throughout the year, including when the Corvettes are tucked away for winter. Social traditions have included euchre nights, the Winter Bash potluck, picnics, and a car show and cookout at Eriksen Chevrolet.

sections.title: Pick your kind of gathering
paragraphs: Some evenings are about cards and conversation; others are about sharing a meal or catching up outdoors. The calendar is the place to find current breakfasts, ice cream runs, and other gatherings.

sections.title: Help make it happen
paragraphs: Members bring ideas and host activities. If you’d like to help organize a social, get in touch with the club or ask at a meeting.

title: Good people, doing good things.
lead: The Corvette brings us together. Helping our neighbors gives us another reason to show up.

sections.title: Giving close to home
paragraphs: MWC’s community work has included raising funds for children facing illness and helping families in the Quad Cities area. Members also rally around one another when support is needed.

sections.title: A history of pitching in
paragraphs: The club’s recorded projects include bicycles and helmets for Toys for Tots, donations to Angel Tree and Coats for Kids, and support for veterans through Vettes on the River. These are examples of the club’s charitable work over the years.

sections.title: Be part of the next effort
paragraphs: Look for charity events on the calendar or contact the charity director to learn where you can help.

title: A small gesture. A shared tradition.
lead: A friendly wave says you’re part of the Corvette family.

sections.title: Recognition on the road
paragraphs: MWC supports the longstanding custom of Corvette drivers greeting one another as they pass. It is a simple way to acknowledge a shared enthusiasm, whether you know the other driver or not.

sections.title: Keep it friendly
paragraphs: If you see another Corvette and it’s safe to do so, offer a wave. A small gesture from the steering wheel is enough. Keep your attention on driving, and don’t worry if the other person misses it.

sections.title: A tradition in print
paragraphs: The club’s original page preserves an article from the August–September 1969 issue of Corvette News and wave etiquette credited to Dan Woomer of Lost Caravan Corvette Club.

title: You’re in. Let’s get you settled.
lead: A few first steps will help you hear the news, meet the people, and make the most of MWC.

sections.title: 01 · Get the club emails
paragraphs: The club uses Mailchimp for member news and updates. Use the existing signup page to add yourself to the club’s mailing list.

sections.title: 02 · Find your way around
paragraphs: Use the existing member website for private club information. Sign in with your username or email and password. If you need to reset your password, use the lost-password option there and check your spam folder for the email.

sections.title: 03 · Put something on the calendar
paragraphs: Come to a meeting, choose an outing, and introduce yourself. A new-member ambassador can help you get acquainted.

title: Part of a bigger Corvette family.
lead: MWC is a charter member of NCCC, connecting our club with fellow enthusiasts around the country.

sections.title: Our national connection
paragraphs: The National Council of Corvette Clubs was founded in 1959 as an all-volunteer organization. Its purpose includes encouraging Corvette ownership and enjoyment, sharing information, and supporting activities among clubs.
Mid-West Corvettes is identified as club MW-054.

sections.title: Membership and information
paragraphs: NCCC membership is part of the MWC application process. Visit the national organization for its current programs, membership details, and event information.

title: The next generation of Corvette fans.
lead: Introduce the younger members of your family to a hobby they can grow with.

sections.title: A Corvette club for kids
paragraphs: The Future Corvette Owners Association is NCCC’s youth organization. It began in 1991 and became the official junior organization in 1992, giving young enthusiasts a way to share in the Corvette hobby.

sections.title: Learn about joining
paragraphs: The club’s introduction describes FCOA for children under 16. Visit the FCOA website for current eligibility, fees, benefits, and application instructions.

title: A day at the races.
lead: Discover the road course that has drawn sports-car enthusiasts for generations.

sections.title: A destination with history
paragraphs: Road America opened in 1955 near Elkhart Lake, Wisconsin. Its original 4.048-mile, 14-turn course follows the area’s natural hills and terrain. The club’s archive includes visits and planning information for this longstanding racing destination.

sections.title: Plan for the event you’re attending
paragraphs: Use Road America’s official site for current racing schedules, tickets, visitor information, and driving programs. The dates on MWC’s original 2023 article are historical.

sections.title: Going with the club?
paragraphs: Check the club calendar or ask at a meeting whether members are planning a trip. Confirm any Corvette Corral parking arrangements with the event organizer before traveling.
